name: Project Week: AI in the Metaverse
description:
The project is aimed at building (and later operating) a virtual society based on Large Language Models (LLMs). As part of the project, students will create a virtual environment in three-dimensional space in which virtual characters based on LLM agents interact with each other in a similar way to people in a society. In addition, the students will design and implement a constitution for the virtual space. At the end of the project week, the virtual space will be released for further interdisciplinary research. The aim is to create a virtual reality that can provide the basis for further testing and research in the field of LLMs as well as interdisciplinary research, particularly in the field of sociology.

The project is interdisciplinary in nature and is aimed at students from various disciplines, in particular, but not exclusively: social sciences, political sciences, computer science, games engineering, architecture, law. Students from non-subject areas can also take part in the project if they are interested in helping to shape the virtual environment and society, as bringing in expertise from other subject areas will promote the project as a whole.

The project participants will be assigned different tasks, which can be assigned to different subject areas.

Game design and 3D modeling: Creation of an environment in virtual space/the “game” design, which will represent the living and action space of the virtual characters and creation of the 3D avatars. Creating the architecture of the virtual buildings in which the interactions between the virtual characters are to take place.

Backend and LLM infrastructure: Programming the basic functions and backend of the virtual environment. This includes basic functions that ensure interaction between characters and between characters and objects. In addition, setting up and programming the LLM infrastructure required to operate the LLMs and make them available to the virtual characters based on these LLMs.

Constitution and legal system: Formulation of a constitution that all members of the virtual society must follow. Checking whether the virtual characters are able to draw up simple legal norms themselves based on the above-mentioned constitution or whether this would (still) have to be done by humans.
prerequisites:
Depending on the technical background and the resulting allocation to the individual project topics, the previous knowledge will also vary depending on the project task.

Game design and 3D modeling: Basic knowledge of game engines/3D engines (the game engine used is expected to be Godot 4.3) and/or confident use of 3D modeling software.

Backend and LLM infrastructure: Confident handling of object-oriented programming languages. The programming language used will mainly be GodotScript. Familiarization with the special features of GodotScript before the start of the project week is sufficient. Students working on the development of the LLM infrastructure require knowledge of machine learning, in particular Python and Pytorch, and ideally also experience in setting up and operating LLMs locally.

Subject area constitution and legal system: None
